Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle Belarusian мѣхъ (měx), from Old East Slavic мѣхъ (měxŭ), from Proto-Slavic *měxъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *maišás, from Proto-Indo-European *moysós (ram, wool).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [mʲex]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

мех • (mjex) m inan (genitive ме́ха, nominative plural мяхі́, genitive plural мяхо́ў)

  1. sack
    Synonym: мяшо́к (mjašók)
  2. fur
    Synonym: фу́тра (fútra)
  3. bellows

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak mech, from Proto-Slavic *měxъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmɛx]
  • Rhymes: -ɛx
  • Hyphenation: мех

Noun

[edit]

мех (mex) m inan (diminutive мещок, augmentative мехиско or мешиско, relational adjective мехов)

  1. sack, bag
    мех кромплї ― mex kromplji ― a sack of potatoes
  2. bellows
    мех на ґайдох ― mex na gajdox ― bellows on bagpipes
  3. goatskin, waterskin
    мех за вино ― mex za vino ― wineskin (literally, “goatskin for wine”)

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
мех
Wikipedia ru

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [mʲex]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Old East Slavic мѣхъ (měxŭ), from Proto-Slavic *měxъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *maišás, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *moysós. Cognates include Ukrainian міх (mix), Belarusian мех (mjex), Old Church Slavonic мѣхъ (měxŭ), Serbo-Croatian мијех/mijeh, Polish miech, Czech měch.

Compare typologically ко́жа (kóža) (<~ коза́ (kozá)); лоси́ны (losíny) (< лось (losʹ)). Also compare English goatskin.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • мѣхъ (měx) — pre-1918 spelling

Noun

[edit]

мех • (mex) m inan (genitive ме́ха, nominative plural меха́, genitive plural мехо́в, relational adjective мехово́й)

  1. fur

Tajik

[edit]
як мех

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Classical Persian میخ (mēx).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /mex/, [meχ]

Noun

[edit]

мех • (mex) (Persian spelling میخ)

  1. nail (A spike-shaped metal fastener)
  2. peg (cylindrical wooden or metal object used to fasten)
